identity.title: Powered Industrial Truck Pre-Shift Inspection Log

scan.summary: This is a daily inspection log for a Toyota forklift (model 8FGU25, unit FL-2, propane-powered) operated at the Portland warehouse. The log documents pre-shift inspections of 17 days in September 2026, tracking 16 specific items required by OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7): tires, forks, mast, horn, lights, belt, brakes, steering, LPG tank, extinguisher, data plate, overhead guard, and seat belt. Each inspection is marked pass (√) or defect (X), with operator initials recorded. Defects must be reported and corrected before use.
scan.freshness_note: The log's last entry is September 17, 2026, which is 12 days old as of today (September 29, 2026). This is recent and current for an ongoing inspection record.

gaps.title: Record continuation after September 17
gaps.description: The log shows inspections through September 17, 2026. No entries appear after that date. This could indicate the log is incomplete for the current month, or the truck was not used after September 17.
gaps.fix: Confirm whether the truck has been in use since September 17. If so, continue the inspection log with daily pre-shift entries. If the truck is in storage, document that status.
gaps.locator: ongoing requirement, not specific to this log
gaps.quote: Truck: Toyota 8FGU25, unit FL-2, propane · Month: September 2026

gaps.title: Details of defects not captured
gaps.description: On September 9, the Horn is marked with X (defect) and the note says 'Horn not working.' However, the log does not record who was assigned to fix it, when it was fixed, or confirmation that the defect was corrected before the truck was returned to service. OSHA 1910.178(q)(7) requires that 'Defects when found shall be immediately reported and corrected.'
gaps.fix: Extend the log format to include: (1) date defect reported to maintenance, (2) expected date of correction, (3) date correction verified. Alternatively, maintain a separate defect log linked by date and unit number. For the Sept 9 horn defect, locate the work order or maintenance record showing the repair and date of completion.
gaps.quote: Defects when found shall be immediately reported and corrected

conditions.title: Daily examination before placing truck in service
conditions.evidence_expected: Inspection log with date, shift, equipment hours, all 16 checklist items marked, and operator initials. Defects noted and documented as corrected.

conditions.title: Truck must not be placed in service if defects exist affecting safety
conditions.evidence_expected: The truck is not operated on days or shifts where a safety-affecting defect is found. For the Sept 9 horn defect, evidence that the truck was either not used that day pending repair, or that the horn defect does not affect safe operation of the truck.

conditions.title: Defects must be immediately reported and corrected
conditions.evidence_expected: Maintenance work orders, repair tickets, or supervisor notes documenting the date defect was reported and the date it was corrected.

expected_missing.title: Operator Training and Evaluation Certificates
expected_missing.why: OSHA 1910.178(l) requires that each operator be trained and evaluated before operating the truck, with re-evaluation at least every three years. The inspection log alone does not provide proof of training.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies maintain operator training records separate from inspection logs

expected_missing.title: Maintenance and Repair Records
expected_missing.why: The log identifies defects (e.g., Sept 9 horn) but does not record what was done to fix them. OSHA 1910.178(q)(7) requires defects to be immediately corrected; a separate maintenance or work order log should document repairs.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies maintain work orders or maintenance logs to close the loop on identified defects

expected_missing.title: Truck Manual and Safety Decal Verification
expected_missing.why: The checklist includes 'Data plate legible' and 'Overhead guard' but does not verify that the operator manual is onboard and legible, which is part of the pre-operation inspection best practice per OSHA guidance.
expected_missing.basis: OSHA eTool and inspection checklists reference operator manual presence as a recommended pre-operation check

scan.confidence_notes: High confidence in what the log records and its compliance status. The document is clear and straightforward: it is a dated, legible, well-maintained inspection log that covers a two-week period with daily entries, operator initials, and one documented defect. The gaps identified are not about the log's quality but about what it does not show: the resolution of the Sept 9 horn defect and continuation of inspections after Sept 17. The OSHA rule (1910.178(q)(7)) is firm and well-established; the interpretation that defects must be reported and corrected immediately is consistent across all sources consulted. No ambiguity was found in what the standard requires or what this log demonstrates. The only uncertainty is whether the log is complete for the month, which is a factual question about the company's current operations, not about the document itself.
